boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Rhodes destinations for studying, gathering, recreation, dining, arts, and quiet outdoor time, verified against the College’s current campus guide and facility information.

cards.title: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.subtitle: Library facilities, Middle Ground, Writing Center & Muslim Prayer Center
cards.notes: Start here when your plan needs several academic supports in one stop; the campus guide lists library facilities, Middle Ground, the Writing Center, and Muslim Prayer Center.
cards.short_summary: A central academic building with multiple listed support and study-oriented destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current campus guide lists Paul Barret, Jr. Library with library facilities, Middle Ground, Muslim Prayer Center, and Writing Center.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Rhodes library and building-access policies.

cards.title: Middle Ground
cards.subtitle: Inside Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Use this named library destination as a meet-up point before settling into library work; confirm current service and seating arrangements when you arrive.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed destination within the Barret Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current campus guide lists Middle Ground within Paul Barret, Jr. Library.
cards.access_notes: Located in the library; access and any food or beverage purchases follow current College policies.

cards.title: Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Inside Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Bring a draft or assignment plan and check the Writing Center’s current appointment or walk-in process before relying on a visit for feedback.
cards.short_summary: A campus writing-support destination listed in the Barret Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current campus guide lists the Writing Center within Paul Barret, Jr. Library.
cards.access_notes: Check current Writing Center availability and library access policies before visiting.

cards.title: Lynx Lair
cards.subtitle: Bryan Campus Life Center
cards.notes: Choose the Lynx Lair for a low-key recreation break with billiards, game rooms, TV viewing, lounge areas, and a snack bar listed by the College.
cards.short_summary: A student recreation area with games, TV viewing, lounges, and a snack bar.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes identifies the L. Palmer Brown Lynx Lair as a student recreation area with a snack bar, billiards, game rooms, TV viewing, and lounge areas.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Bryan Campus Life Center; snack-bar items may require purchase and access may be limited to the Rhodes community.

cards.title: Bryan Campus Life Center
cards.subtitle: Fitness, recreation, and campus-event facilities
cards.notes: Use the BCLC as a hub for a workout or recreation plan; its listed facilities include courts, a fitness room, indoor track, pool, and event spaces.
cards.short_summary: A multi-purpose campus life and recreation facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes says the Bryan Campus Life Center includes athletic and fitness facilities, a fitness room, indoor jogging track, courts, pool, and space for student social events and lectures.
cards.access_notes: Use follows current recreation-facility and building-access policies.

cards.entity_name: Brenda and Lester Crain Reception Hall
cards.title: Crain Reception Hall
cards.subtitle: Bryan Campus Life Center
cards.notes: Check the campus events calendar or a registered organization’s plans for scheduled gatherings in this named BCLC reception hall before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A named BCLC venue for campus social events and special occasions.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes describes the Brenda and Lester Crain Reception Hall as accommodating campus social events and other special occasions.
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on event scheduling and College access rules.

cards.title: McCallum Ballroom
cards.subtitle: Bryan Campus Life Center
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled lecture, performance, organization event, or campus occasion using this named ballroom; access depends on the individual event.
cards.short_summary: A named ballroom in Rhodes’ campus life center.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current campus guide lists McCallum Ballroom in the Bryan Campus Life Center, and the College describes the center as accommodating student social events, lectures, and other campus occasions.
cards.access_notes: Event access, registration, and any ticketing are determined by the organizer.

cards.title: Clough-Hanson Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: S. DeWitt Clough Hall
cards.notes: Add the gallery to an arts-focused walk and check its current exhibition information before visiting; the College maps it in S. DeWitt Clough Hall.
cards.short_summary: A named campus art gallery in S. DeWitt Clough Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current campus guide lists the Clough-Hanson Art Gallery in S. DeWitt Clough Hall.
cards.access_notes: Check current exhibition hours and building access before visiting.

cards.title: Hubert F. Fisher Memorial Garden
cards.subtitle: Campus garden with named labyrinth and meditation gardens
cards.notes: Build in a quiet outdoor pause here; the campus guide identifies the Fisher Memorial Garden alongside the Burns Memorial Labyrinth and two meditation gardens.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed garden area with a labyrinth and meditation gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current campus guide lists Hubert F. Fisher Memorial Garden, Adrienne McMillan Burns Memorial Labyrinth, Claire Markham Collins Meditation Garden, and James H. Daughdrill Jr. Meditation Garden.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access is subject to campus conditions and College policies.

cards.title: Catherine Burrow Refectory
cards.subtitle: Tina McWhorter Dining Room & Wilson Fireside Lounge
cards.notes: Use the Refectory as a dining-plan anchor, then note its listed rooms and lounge when arranging a meal or on-campus meeting around building traffic.
cards.short_summary: Rhodes’ main dining facility, with several named rooms and a fireside lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes identifies Catherine Burrow Refectory as the College’s main dining facility; its current campus guide lists the Tina McWhorter Dining Room and Wilson Fireside Lounge there.
cards.access_notes: Dining access and meal purchases follow current Rhodes Dining Services policies.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Free, under-21-safe places and activities in Memphis with direct access or admission evidence.

cards.title: See contemporary art at Clough-Hanson Gallery
cards.subtitle: Clough Hall · Rhodes College
cards.notes: Plan a gallery stop during its Tuesday–Saturday public hours. Check the exhibition calendar before heading to Clough Hall.
cards.short_summary: A free, public Rhodes gallery for rotating contemporary-art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes states that admission to Clough-Hanson Gallery is free; it is open Tuesday through Saturday, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Clough-Hanson Gallery Exhibition Highlights the Exceptional Work of Rhodes Art Professor David McCarthy
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm an exhibition is on view before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Dixon galleries and gardens
cards.subtitle: 4339 Park Avenue · Memphis
cards.notes: Meet at the Dixon for a self-paced art-and-garden walk. Use its visit page to confirm the day’s gallery and garden hours.
cards.short_summary: Art exhibitions and designed gardens at a museum that identifies itself as free.
cards.evidence_claim: Dixon Gallery & Gardens describes itself as a free art museum and public garden in Memphis.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Friday and Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Sunday 1–5 p.m.; closed Mondays. Verify holiday changes.

cards.entity_name: Art Museum of the University of Memphis
cards.title: Browse the Art Museum of the University of Memphis
cards.subtitle: 3750 Norriswood Avenue · University of Memphis
cards.notes: Set aside time for the Egyptian, African, and changing galleries. Contact the museum if a temporary-exhibition change affects access.
cards.short_summary: A university art museum with permanent and temporary galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: The Art Museum of the University of Memphis states that admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Visit the Art Museum of the University of Memphis
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Saturday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed on university holidays and between temporary exhibitions.

cards.entity_name: Martha and Robert Fogelman Galleries of Contemporary Art
cards.title: Visit the Fogelman Galleries
cards.subtitle: Art and Communication Building · University of Memphis
cards.notes: Use the paired galleries for a short contemporary-art conversation. Enter through the Art and Communication Building on Central Avenue.
cards.short_summary: Two contemporary-art galleries on the University of Memphis main campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fogelman Galleries state that admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Visit the Martha and Robert Fogelman Galleries of Contemporary Art
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed on university holidays and between exhibitions.

cards.title: Catch the free Saturday morning at Brooks
cards.subtitle: 1934 Poplar Avenue · Overton Park
cards.notes: Arrive during the museum’s stated Saturday free-admission window, then choose a few galleries to discuss before your time is up.
cards.short_summary: A timed, free Saturday visit to Memphis’s art museum in Overton Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Memphis Brooks Museum of Art states that it is free every Saturday from 10 a.m. to noon.
cards.access_notes: Free only Saturdays, 10 a.m.–noon; check the museum’s visit information for closures or schedule changes.

cards.title: Spread out on the Greensward
cards.subtitle: Overton Park · Memphis
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or a low-key game and meet on Overton Park’s signature open space. Leave the space ready for the next group.
cards.short_summary: Overton Park’s main open lawn for an unstructured outdoor hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Overton Park Conservancy identifies the Greensward as its signature open space and says the park is always free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The park is open daily from dawn to dusk; the park has no admission fee.

cards.title: Take a slow lap through the Formal Gardens
cards.subtitle: Overton Park · Memphis
cards.notes: Use the symmetrical garden paths for a quiet walk and conversation. Keep to paths and treat plantings as viewing-only.
cards.short_summary: A named garden area within Overton Park for a calm outdoor meet-up.
cards.evidence_claim: Overton Park Conservancy lists the Formal Gardens as a park feature and states the park is always free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The park is open daily from dawn to dusk; the park has no admission fee.

cards.title: Walk the Old Forest trails
cards.subtitle: Overton Park · Memphis
cards.notes: Choose a daylight trail loop with a friend and stay on marked paths. The Conservancy lists more than eight miles of trails in the park.
cards.short_summary: Protected old-growth forest trails inside Overton Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Overton Park Conservancy identifies the Old Forest State Natural Area as 126 acres of protected old-growth forest and states the park is always free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The park is open daily from dawn to dusk; the park has no admission fee.

cards.title: Pause at Veterans Plaza
cards.subtitle: Overton Park · Memphis
cards.notes: Meet at the plaza and take in its memorials before continuing through the park. Keep the visit reflective and respect the monuments.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated memorial area within Overton Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Overton Park Conservancy lists Veterans Plaza among park features and states the park is always free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The park is open daily from dawn to dusk; the park has no admission fee.

cards.title: Take a no-cost park walk at Shelby Farms
cards.subtitle: 6903 Great View Drive North · Memphis
cards.notes: Pick a trail, lake, or green space and build your own walking loop. Paid rentals and ticketed activities are separate from park entry.
cards.short_summary: A large Memphis park with trails, lakes, and green spaces open to the community.
cards.evidence_claim: Shelby Farms Park states that it is free and open to the community.
cards.source_title: Join the Herd | Shelby Farms Park
cards.access_notes: Park entry is free; rentals and certain park-produced events may have separate charges.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Rhodes study environments, spanning a 24-hour library area, small group rooms, academic-support spaces, and specialized work settings.

cards.title: Middle Ground
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Use this library study area when your work runs past normal building hours; bring your Lynx Card and confirm any term-specific access updates.
cards.short_summary: Rhodes identifies Middle Ground as its 24-hour study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Barret Library lists Middle Ground as a 24-hour study space.
cards.access_notes: The library’s official page identifies Middle Ground as 24-hour study space; confirm current campus-card access rules before going.

cards.title: Study Room 120
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Use this named group-study room for a focused working session; check with the library for room availability and any reservation or entry requirements.
cards.short_summary: A current Rhodes room listing identifies Barret 120 as a study room.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 120 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. Availability, reservations, and building access are not stated in the room listing; verify before use.

cards.title: Study Room 222
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Make this a meet-up point for shared reading or problem sets, then confirm with library staff whether the room is open or reservable that day.
cards.short_summary: A named second-floor library study room documented by Rhodes.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 222 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. The listing does not state reservation procedures or public access rules; confirm before use.

cards.title: Study Room 224
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Choose this numbered library room for a contained group work block; ask the Check-Out Desk about availability before moving your materials in.
cards.short_summary: A specifically identified Barret Library group-study option.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 224 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library; the library lists group study rooms among its services. Confirm room availability and any booking rules.

cards.title: Study Room 230
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Set up here for a collaborative assignment or review session, and verify its availability with the library rather than relying on a posted schedule.
cards.short_summary: A named Barret Library study room on the current Rhodes listing.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 230 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. The available source does not give booking details, so check with the library before using it.

cards.title: Study Room 308
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Bring a small team and a clear agenda for this designated study room; confirm access and whether a reservation is needed before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A numbered library study room documented in current Rhodes materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 308 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. Confirm room availability, reservation policy, and building access with library staff.

cards.title: Study Room 310
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Use the named room for a collaborative work session, but check its status first; the official listing confirms the room, not a standing booking schedule.
cards.short_summary: A specifically listed study room within Barret Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 310 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. No public booking details were verified; contact the library to confirm access before use.

cards.title: Language Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Palmer Hall
cards.notes: Bring language coursework or digital assignments to use large-screen computer stations, charging, printing, and flexible work areas; reserve group space directly.
cards.short_summary: Flexible work space with large-screen computer stations and student-group reservations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Language Learning Center lists flexible study/work spaces, large-screen computer stations, charging, printing, and reservable student-group space.
cards.access_notes: Student-group and event space is reservable through the Language Center; its page directs students to contact the Center’s RSA.

cards.title: Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Barret Library, Room 122
cards.notes: Bring a draft at any stage for a writing-focused session; students can drop in for an impromptu appointment or sign up through the Writing Center.
cards.short_summary: A Barret Library writing-support space for scheduled or drop-in work.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes states that the Writing Center is in Barret Library Room 122 and that students may drop in or sign up for a session.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Barret Library in Room 122. Drop-in availability is not guaranteed; students may also sign up through the Writing Center.

cards.title: Testing Room
cards.subtitle: Barret Library, Room 303
cards.notes: Students with approved testing accommodations can reserve a distraction-limited carrel, computer, or height-adjustable station for an accommodated exam session.
cards.short_summary: A reservation-based, distraction-limited setting for eligible accommodated testing.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes describes Room 303 as a fob-accessible, distraction-limited testing space with 14 carrels, five computers, and two height-adjustable stations for eligible students.
cards.access_notes: Fob access is limited to Rhodes students with approved Student Accessibility Services testing accommodations; reserve a space for each test.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named cultural and recreation destinations in the Overton Park corridors immediately south of Rhodes College.

cards.title: Overton Park
cards.subtitle: Poplar Avenue corridor, south of Rhodes College
cards.notes: Enter from Poplar Avenue and use the park map to choose a cultural stop, trail, or open-space route before continuing through Midtown.
cards.short_summary: A 342-acre Midtown park with cultural and outdoor destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: Memphis Parks identifies Overton Park as a 342-acre Midtown park containing trails, the Shell, zoo, golf course, Rainbow Lake, Veterans Plaza, and Greensward.
cards.access_notes: Use the park’s posted seasonal hours when planning an outdoor visit.

cards.title: Old Forest State Natural Area
cards.subtitle: Poplar Avenue / Overton Park corridor, south of Rhodes College
cards.notes: Take the marked Old Forest Loop for a wooded walk; bring water and stay on established paths to protect the natural area.
cards.short_summary: Protected urban old-growth forest with marked walking routes.
cards.evidence_claim: Memphis Parks states that the Old Forest has a 1.4-mile limestone running trail, over a mile of paved trails, and four miles of unpaved walking paths.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor trail access; use the park’s posted seasonal hours.

cards.title: Overton Park Shell
cards.subtitle: Veterans Plaza Drive corridor, Overton Park
cards.notes: Check the Shell’s program before you go, then pair a scheduled outdoor performance with a walk through the surrounding park paths.
cards.short_summary: Historic outdoor concert venue inside Overton Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes College identifies the Overton Park Shell as an outdoor music venue and notes that it offers free programming.
cards.access_notes: Event availability varies; confirm the current program with the venue before traveling.

cards.title: Memphis Brooks Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Poplar Avenue corridor, Overton Park
cards.notes: Plan around the gallery schedule and use the museum’s directions from Poplar Avenue; Saturday morning admission is listed as free.
cards.short_summary: Art museum in Overton Park with exhibitions and visitor programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum states that it is at 1934 Poplar Avenue in Overton Park and offers free admission every Saturday from 10 a.m. to noon.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Memphis Brooks Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: General admission is ticketed outside the listed free Saturday morning period; check the museum’s current visit page.

cards.title: Memphis Zoo
cards.subtitle: Prentiss Place corridor, Overton Park
cards.notes: Use the zoo’s visitor information to plan an animal-focused outing, and allow time for the walk between exhibits rather than rushing the route.
cards.short_summary: Accredited zoo located within Overton Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Memphis Zoo lists its street address as 2000 Prentiss Place, Memphis, TN 38112.
cards.access_notes: Admission is required; review current tickets and visitor rules before arrival.

cards.title: Overton Park 9
cards.subtitle: Poplar Avenue / Veterans Plaza Drive corridor, Overton Park
cards.notes: Reserve a tee time if you want to play, or stop by the clubhouse area while exploring the park’s Poplar Avenue-side attractions.
cards.short_summary: Nine-hole public golf course and clubhouse in Overton Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Memphis Parks describes Overton Park 9 as a 48-acre, nine-hole golf course with a clubhouse, restrooms, concessions, and parking.
cards.access_notes: Playing requires a tee-time reservation; call the listed golf-course number for current hours.

cards.title: Rainbow Lake Playground
cards.subtitle: Veterans Plaza Drive corridor, Overton Park
cards.notes: Make this a daylight stop while walking the park loop, and use the nearby paths to connect toward the Shell or other park destinations.
cards.short_summary: Named playground destination beside Rainbow Lake in Overton Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Overton Park Conservancy identifies Rainbow Lake Playground among the park’s cultural and natural attractions.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-space access; use the park’s posted seasonal hours.

cards.title: East Parkway Playground
cards.subtitle: East Parkway North corridor, Overton Park
cards.notes: Use this named playground as an East Parkway-side waypoint, then continue on the park paths toward the Old Forest or cultural venues.
cards.short_summary: Named playground at Overton Park’s East Parkway side.
cards.evidence_claim: Memphis Parks lists two playgrounds among the features on the Overton Park grounds.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-space access; use the park’s posted seasonal hours.

cards.title: Overton Bark
cards.subtitle: East Parkway North / Overton Park corridor
cards.notes: If you are visiting with a dog, use the designated fenced areas and follow the posted size separation and on-site rules.
cards.short_summary: Fenced dog-park destination within Overton Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Memphis Parks describes Overton Bark as a dog park with two fenced spaces separated for dogs 25 pounds or less and dogs 25 pounds or more.
cards.access_notes: Bring a dog only if using the dog park; use the park’s posted seasonal hours.

cards.title: Bike Gate
cards.subtitle: East Parkway North corridor, Overton Park
cards.notes: Use the Bike Gate plaza as a recognizable arrival point for the park, then follow the map toward the Old Forest, Shell, or museum.
cards.short_summary: Named sculpture-and-plaza landmark at Overton Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Overton Park Conservancy identifies the Bike Gate sculpture and plaza as a park feature.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-space access; use the park’s posted seasonal hours.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Rhodes rituals, recurring events, and campus customs.

cards.title: Sign the Honor Code
cards.subtitle: First-year ceremony at Rhodes College
cards.notes: During Welcome Week, attend the formal pledge-signing ceremony and reflect on the community commitment to honesty, respect, and accountability.
cards.short_summary: First-years annually sign a pledge supporting Rhodes’ Honor System.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes states that first-year students annually sign an Honor Code pledge each fall, committing to uphold the Honor System.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Welcome Week; consult the current program for attendance details.

cards.title: Give the Seal a Wide Berth
cards.subtitle: Cloister of Southwestern Hall
cards.notes: Find the seal in Southwestern Hall’s Cloister, observe the longstanding superstition, and save crossing it for the senior Commencement procession.
cards.short_summary: A graduation superstition reserves crossing the Cloister seal for seniors.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes says tradition holds that stepping on the seal delays graduation, while seniors cross it during the Commencement march.
cards.source_title: 100 Years in Memphis: A Long History Makes for Meaningful—and Fun—Traditions | Rhodes News
cards.access_notes: Located inside Southwestern Hall; follow building access rules and do not obstruct ceremonies.

cards.title: Graduate in Fisher Garden
cards.subtitle: Hubert F. Fisher Memorial Garden
cards.notes: At Commencement, join the senior class in the garden ceremony after processing through Southwestern Hall, then celebrate respectfully with family and classmates.
cards.short_summary: Fisher Garden is the historic setting for Rhodes senior graduations.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes says seniors have historically graduated in Fisher Garden and its 2025 graduates received diplomas there.
cards.access_notes: This is part of the official Commencement program for graduating students and guests.

cards.title: Take a Pancake Study Break
cards.subtitle: Catherine Burrow Refectory during finals
cards.notes: When finals arrive, pause your studying for the semester’s pancake event, where faculty and staff volunteers help serve the campus community.
cards.short_summary: A finals-week breakfast brings faculty, staff, and students together.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes documents a late-night pancake breakfast on the Sunday before finals, led by faculty and staff volunteers.
cards.source_title: 100 Years in Memphis: A Long History Makes for Meaningful—and Fun—Traditions | Rhodes News
cards.access_notes: The cited 2025 account listed 9:30–11:30 p.m.; confirm the current finals-week schedule.

cards.title: Watch a Whiteball Rally
cards.subtitle: Whiteball Court beside Gordon White Residence Hall
cards.notes: Visit the dedicated court to see Rhodes’ handball-like pastime, played against the slate roof of the passage connecting White Hall and the Refectory.
cards.short_summary: Whiteball uses a distinctive campus roof as part of play.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes identifies Whiteball as a decades-long favorite pastime played using the slate roof between White Hall and the Refectory.
cards.access_notes: Use the designated court and be considerate of nearby residence and dining traffic.

cards.entity_name: Society of Physics Students Pumpkin Drop
cards.title: See the Pumpkin Drop
cards.subtitle: Annual Rhodes physics fair
cards.notes: Attend the Society of Physics Students’ annual fair for hands-on demonstrations, then watch the group’s pumpkin experiment from the designated viewing area.
cards.short_summary: Physics students pair interactive science demonstrations with a pumpkin-drop experiment.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes describes the Pumpkin Drop as an annual Society of Physics Students fair with demonstrations and frozen pumpkins dropped from Rhodes Tower.
cards.source_title: 100 Years in Memphis: A Long History Makes for Meaningful—and Fun—Traditions | Rhodes News
cards.access_notes: Attend only during the organized event and follow all staff safety directions and viewing boundaries.

cards.title: Spot the Lynx-Statue Ritual
cards.subtitle: Rhodes College campus
cards.notes: Find the campus lynx statue and photograph it from the ground; Rhodes’ traditions story notes students try to climb onto it throughout the year.
cards.short_summary: The lynx statue has become the focus of a playful student ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes reports that students try to climb onto the lynx statue throughout the year, while joking that it is a required graduation ritual.
cards.source_title: 100 Years in Memphis: A Long History Makes for Meaningful—and Fun—Traditions | Rhodes News
cards.access_notes: Observe and photograph from the ground; do not climb the statue or damage campus property.

cards.title: Catch Rites of Spring
cards.subtitle: Annual student-organized concert series
cards.notes: Look for the annual concert series and its Battle of the Bands, which gives student performers a chance to open for the featured artist.
cards.short_summary: A student initiative grew into an annual campus concert tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes says Rites of Spring evolved from a student initiative into an annual concert series featuring a Battle of the Bands.
cards.source_title: 100 Years in Memphis: A Long History Makes for Meaningful—and Fun—Traditions | Rhodes News
cards.access_notes: Event timing, venue, and entry details vary; use the current Rhodes events information.

cards.title: Meet the Finals Fairies
cards.subtitle: Popular Rhodes study areas during finals
cards.notes: Keep an eye out in study spaces during finals for Student Life’s surprise snack visits, staffed by faculty and staff in character costumes.
cards.short_summary: Surprise finals-week visits deliver snacks and a bit of levity to study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes states that Student Life arranges Finals Fairies surprise visits to popular study areas with snacks and costumed faculty and staff volunteers.
cards.source_title: 100 Years in Memphis: A Long History Makes for Meaningful—and Fun—Traditions | Rhodes News
cards.access_notes: Occurs during finals in selected study spaces; preserve a quiet study environment.

cards.title: Mark LDOC
cards.subtitle: End-of-semester Rhodes celebration
cards.notes: After the semester’s final class day, join the campus activities offered for LDOC, which have included crafts, dunk tanks, and bounce houses.
cards.short_summary: LDOC turns the last day of classes into an activity-filled campus celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes identifies LDOC as a celebration of the last day of classes each semester, with activities ranging from DIY crafts to dunk tanks and bounce houses.
cards.source_title: 100 Years in Memphis: A Long History Makes for Meaningful—and Fun—Traditions | Rhodes News
cards.access_notes: Programming changes by semester; check current Student Life announcements.
